title: Java can now run 10,000 threads without breaking a sweat
description:
Platform threads cost real OS memory -- a few thousand and your JVM starts choking. Java 21's virtual threads change the math entirely: millions of them can exist at once because they only occupy a real OS thread while actively running. Ordinary blocking code, like Thread.sleep or a JDBC call, just works with no reactive rewrite. This is one slice of a full lesson on advanced Java concurrency, covering CompletableFuture chaining and structured concurrency too.

Source lesson:
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/java-mastery-path/level-4/03-advanced-concurrency-patterns/

#Shorts

beats.narration: A single OS thread costs real memory. Spin up more than a few thousand platform threads and your JVM starts choking. Java's virtual threads change that completely.
Here's ten thousand tasks, each one running on its own virtual thread, each one calling a blocking Thread.sleep. In the old world, that alone would crash your JVM.

The trick: when a virtual thread blocks on I/O, the JVM unmounts it from the real OS thread underneath, and that thread goes and runs someone else's work. Ordinary blocking code, like a database call or an HTTP request, just works, no reactive rewrite needed.

display.heading: Unmounted while blocked, remounted when ready
display.subheading: The JVM frees the carrier thread the moment a virtual thread blocks on I/O

beats.narration: That's how you get millions of lightweight threads instead of thousands of expensive ones. Full lesson and code below.
